incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.8, ss. 2(1), 6(1), 9(1). No federal limited partnership registry exists; the Limited Partnership is formed provincially and is then given a federal existence for tax and payroll purposes through a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Directorate; Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online for federal tax payroll accounts
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, together with CRA Business Registration Online application for a federal Business Number
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit requirement. Capital contributions are fixed by the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be cash, property or services; non-resident ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [NAME] LIMITED PARTNERSHIP

The General Partner, acting under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act and the Limited Partnership Agreement, resolves: (1) to accept the capital contributions listed in Schedule A and admit the subscriber as initial Limited Partner; (2) to fix the registered office at [Address], Toronto, Ontario, and appoint [Agent] as agent for service; (3) to appoint [Name] Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary of the General Partner, each authorized to sign filings, tax registrations and banking documents; (4) to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership and complete incidental registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search using the online Ontario Corporate Registry through a licensed search house or directly through ServiceOntario. The proposed name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and must not be confusingly similar to existing corporate, LP, or trade names. Supply a completed Name Reservation Request and retain the search report for registration.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report or Ontario initial notice search result
Written consent from objecting party (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or refused, resubmit an amended name reservation with a new search report; respond to any Examination Officer's objections within 15 days and, if required, obtain consent/coexistence agreement from the conflicting nameholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner acting under the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement detailing capital contributions, allocations, decision-making, restrictions on transfer, dissolution and non-resident ownership. Complete Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership with names of partners, contributions, registered office and principal business address, and verify general partner eligibility.
required_dossiers: Consent and certificate of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting deficiencies by supplemental schedule or amended schedule before filing; no registry action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Partners' Resolution and Registered Office Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and initial Limited Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a valid initial partners' meeting or execute unanimous written resolution adopting capital subscriptions, the registered office, officers of the general partner, and authorizing the filing and banking arrangements. Record in the minute book.
required_dossiers: First governing resolution (unanimous written consent or meeting minutes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is challenged, cure by executing a unanimous written resolution retroactively confirming the actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Declaration and Registry Indexing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership via ServiceOntario's online portal or in person/mail, pay the prescribed C$60 registration fee (approx. US$45), and obtain the confirmation/acknowledgement indexing the LP in the Ontario registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ServiceOntario issues a Notice of Query, respond within the specified period (usually 30 days) with amended information; if rejected, invoke the registrar's reconsideration or resubmit the declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Payroll Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the LP acknowledgement and general partner identification, apply online for a federal Business Number (BN), a payroll deductions account under the Income Tax Act, a GST/HST account (where applicable), and a provincial employer health tax account where payroll exceeds thresholds. This establishes the federal tax administrative existence for the EOR platform.
required_dossiers: General partner identification and CRA internal access
Completed Business Registration Online application (or Form RC1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA holds processing for lack of information, reply to the CRA letter within the stated deadline and provide Form RC59 (Business Consent) if the applicant is not the owner.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); digital portal: CRA My Business Account (MyBA) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html; Business Registration Online (BRO) and the integrated federal-provincial Business Registration Service (BRS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Pre-registration: prepare the limited partnership agreement, extra-provincial registration certificate or original certificate of limited partnership, each partner's fiscal residence statement, and for each foreign partner its foreign tax identifier and corporate registry extract. 2. Apply through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or the Business Registration Service (BRS); the CRA assigns a 9-digit Business Number (BN) to the LP itself, and the LP opens program accounts under that BN: RT (GST/HST) and RP (payroll source deductions for Canadian employees engaged through the EOR platform). 3. For paper filing, submit Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' with the partnership agreement and partner authorizations; foreign first-time applicants may be required to appoint a Canadian resident agent/representative for service of notices. 4. Complete RP account activation to assume statutory employer obligations (Canadian income tax, CPP, EI withholding and remittance). 5. Assess the small-supplier threshold; if worldwide taxable supplies (including associates) exceed CAD 30,000 in a trailing four-quarter period, RT registration is compulsory and GST/HST returns must be filed (electronically once annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 10 million). 6. Open a Canadian bank account, provide CRA direct-deposit details, and register for CRA My Payment or pre-authorized debit for remittances. 7. Annually file the T5013 Partnership Information Return (generally due March 31; a deadline extension to May 1 may apply where all partners are Canadian residents); each partner reports its allocable share on its own return, and a non-resident partner is taxable under Part I on Canadian-source partnership income, with treaty relief available where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A limited partnership created under Canadian law is not an income-tax taxpayer; its income, gains, losses and credits flow through to partners under section 96 of the Income Tax Act. The LP is, however, a separate 'person' for GST/HST purposes and is the mandatory GST/HST registrant in its own name. A limited partner's deductible losses are restricted to the partner's at-risk amount under ITA s. 96(2.1), and the partnership is subject to specified allocation and reporting rules under ITA s. 96 and s. 233.3. Provincial/territorial income taxes and employer health taxes (e.g., Ontario EHT) apply at the applicable provincial level where the LP has permanent establishment or payroll presence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — central bank and monetary authority; prudential banking supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/CFT transaction reporting to FINTRAC; cross-border currency declaration to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility (IMF Article VIII). The Canadian dollar floats freely and there are no exchange controls, approval requirements, or surrender obligations on capital inflows or outflows. The Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) fixes CAD as legal tender. Profit repatriation to non-resident limited partners is unrestricted at the FX level but Part XIII withholding tax of 25% (treaty-reducible) applies to income distributions; a return of capital is not subject to Part XIII withholding. Inbound capital subscriptions require no tax or exchange-control pre-clearance; an Investment Canada Act notification may be triggered where the subscription results in acquisition of control of a Canadian business (not applicable to a newly formed LP unless thresholds are met).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender and no mandatory CAD conversion timeline; receipts may be held in foreign currency. However, under the PCMLTFA, physical cross-border movements of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to CBSA, and financial institutions must file EFT reports to FINTRAC on wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. EOR service receipts must be documented under the Income Tax Act and supported by OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation for deductible cross-border fees.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium as a secondary disbursement rail; not viable as the primary treasury/escrow bank. Canada does not recognize the EU EMI licence; non-resident digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) must register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and, under the Retail Payment Activities Act (effective 2024, supervised by the Bank of Canada), obtain a retail payment licence. MSBs may not take deposits, issue guarantees, or settle like a bank, and client funds must be safeguarded at a Schedule I bank. Wise is practical for low-value global contractor payroll payouts at mid-market FX; capital injections, CRA statutory source deductions, and institutional escrow must clear through a Canadian chartered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted by regulation. FINTRAC allows identity verification without physical presence through dual-process methods (e.g., credit-bureau file match, dual-source database verification, or video credential validation). For a Limited Partnership with non-resident general partners, Big-5 banks in practice require: (1) video KYC interview of every authorized signatory/general partner representative; (2) notarized or apostilled certified copies of passports, partnership registry abstracts, and formation documents; (3) a Canadian legal opinion covering LP authority, ownership chain, and UBO identification; and (4) frequently an in-branch appearance by one partner or a pre-existing banker relationship. Remote-only opening is achievable through the bank's commercial/global desk where Canadian counsel co-conducts verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through LP with non-resident partners creates opaque beneficial-ownership (UBO) chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provincial certificate of limited partnership; up-to-date partnership register with full legal names, residential/tax jurisdictions, and exact percentage interests of all partners; UBO declaration addressing every 25%+ controlling partner; executed LP agreement and amendments; general partner's certificate of incorporation, register of directors, and shareholder register; one-page entity structure diagram with ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EOR payroll flows to dozens of individual beneficiaries across many jurisdictions appear inconsistent with declared operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master Services Agreements with EOR client employers; underlying worker employment contracts and onboarding records; monthly payroll registers and settlement statements; commercial invoices; ISIC 7810 / NAICS 561330 licensing evidence; CRA payroll program account registration and remittance history; documented anti-fraud payroll verification controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, sudden inbound wires classified as capital calls may trigger source-of-funds review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dated capital call notices; LP contribution schedules; subscription agreements and private-placement/registration exemption filings (where applicable); source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations signed by each contributing partner; contributor bank statements evidencing the wealth origin; general partner board/management resolutions and tax clearance notes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wires referencing offshore booking centres or digital-asset origin raise sanctions and reputational flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance narrative evidencing real Canadian staffing and payroll infrastructure; commercial rationale memoranda; underlying client EOR invoices and time-sheet reports; partner statements of background and business purpose; independent AML screening outputs (e.g., World-Check); confirmation that no sanctioned jurisdiction receives funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed FX forwards/swaps flagged as speculative derivative activity rather than hedging
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury risk-management policy limiting instruments to hedging of forecast payroll and receivables exposure; LP agreement treasury mandate; general partner resolutions authorizing specific counterparties and limits; currency exposure schedules mapped to monthly payroll liabilities; bank confirmations that derivatives are end-user hedges under ISDA/CSA.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: SWIFT MT103 from the contributor's foreign bank to the LP's CAD/USD operational account at a Schedule I bank. Field 50K must display the contributor's exact registered name matching KYC; field 59 must display the LP's registered name and account number exactly as opened. Message reference must state: 'Capital Contribution — LP Agreement dated [date] — ISIC 7810 Global EOR Platform'. No exchange-control approval is required; the bank's compliance team clears via OFAC/UN/OSFI watchlist screening, UBO matching against the partnership register, and a source-of-funds hold for amounts ≥ CAD 100,000. For escrow-funded structures, pre-notify the receiving branch with a 20-day advance arrival advice and original contribution documents. Structuring inbound funds into multiple transfers below CAD 10,000 is prohibited as 'structuring' under PCMLTFA and a criminal offence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103/MT202 for cross-border trade settlements (EOR service fees, contractor payroll); Payments Canada ACSS (ACH) for domestic CAD payroll and CRA source-deduction remittances; Lynx (RTGS) for same-day large-value CAD settlements; U.S.-dollar clearing through the Schedule I bank's internal U.S. clearing network (e.g., RBC via RBC Bank, Georgia; BMO via BMO Harris). Commercial letters of credit: issued/confirmed under UCP600 via SWIFT MT700 for high-value staffing service contracts. Every wire ≥ CAD 10,000 is reported by the bank to FINTRAC as an EFT report and must carry the commercial invoice or payroll register reference in the payment narrative.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD OTC forward contracts (tenors ≤ 12 months) for payroll and receivables hedging — exempt from mandatory clearing for a below-threshold non-financial counterparty
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market payroll currencies (INR, PHP, BRL, MXN) where CAD is the reference/underlying currency
OTC vanilla currency options (CAD/USD, EUR/CAD) with upfront premium, limited to hedging of committed EOR receivables
Cross-currency swaps (currency swaps) for long-dated USD-CAD asset/liability matching under the LP treasury policy
FX swaps (rollover swaps against USD) for short-term liquidity management, documented under an executed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Limited Partnership Declaration (Statement of Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Limited Partnership Registry where the LP is registered (e.g., Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta; extra-provincial registration rules apply to a federal-jurisdiction LP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each annual registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of C$20 per day up to C$200; two consecutive years of default trigger administrative strike-off/cancellation of LP registration, converting the partnership to a general partnership and exposing limited partners to unlimited liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013) with partner slips and declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of C$25 per day (minimum C$100; maximum C$2,500); repeated late filing increases to C$50 per day; gross negligence penalty of 5% of unreported income plus 5% per month for up to 12 months; CRA may reassess partners individually.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Transparency Register / UBO Confirmation Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial registrar operating a beneficial ownership transparency registry (British Columbia, Quebec, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) or Corporations Canada once the federal registry is proclaimed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Annual Limited Partnership Declaration (same 60-day anniversary window); any change in an individual with significant control must be reported within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to C$5,000 (BC) and C$25,000 (Quebec) for knowingly false or omitted filings; persistent non-compliance causes registry strike-off and can disqualify the general partner from acting as a licensee in EOR employment agency licensing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a non-offering limited partnership under federal or provincial law; however, an independent audit is triggered if (i) the LP agreement or lenders so require, (ii) the partnership is a 'large partnership' under the Income Tax Act (gross revenue exceeding C$10 million) and CRA requests verification, (iii) a provincial employment agency / EOR licence application demands audited financial statements, or (iv) the LP issues securities or becomes a reporting issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board (AcSB) for publicly accountable enterprises; private LPs may elect ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II); for a global EOR payroll platform, IFRS 15 (revenue from client contracts), IFRS 16 (leases), and IAS 19 (employee benefits) are the operative standards. T5013 tax-basis reconciliation and Canadian partnership allocations (ITA 96) are computed separately from GAAP/ASPE book income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Federally, the LP is subject to the pending federal beneficial ownership registry (Bill C-42; Budget 2024); until proclamation, the LP must maintain an in-house register of individuals with significant control (ISC) and file annual UBO confirmation through the applicable provincial transparency registry (BC, Quebec, Saskatchewan, Manitoba). Any transfer of limited partnership interests — including assignments of one-managed EOR platform equity — must be recorded in the Register of Limited Partners and the ISC register concurrently, with annual confirmation annexed to the LP's declaration. The general partner is liable for register accuracy; knowingly false declarations can lead to fines of up to C$200,000 for the corporate general partner and personal penalties for individual partners.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: C$350–C$850 per year (US$260–US$630) for registered office and resident agent services depending on province
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: C$10,000–C$30,000 (US$7,400–US$22,000) for a full IFRS audit of a mid-size cross-border EOR payroll LP; review engagement C$4,000–C$9,000 (US$3,000–US$6,700)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal Part I general corporate income tax rate; the Canada limited partnership is fiscally transparent and the 15% rate is applied at the partner level on allocable Canadian-source business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 9% preferential Small Business Deduction rate for qualifying active business income allocated to eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation partners; 50% refundable SR&ED investment tax credits for qualifying CCPC partners; no statutory tax holiday exists for Employer of Record payroll services; unreasonable wage and service fees are denied under Income Tax Act s. 67 and s. 247.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) and T5013 Partnership Information Return; filed electronically through CRA My Business Account Web Forms or XML EFILE by a registered E-filer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; each fiscal period normally 12 months.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2/T5013 must be filed within six months after the fiscal period end; Part I federal tax balance is due within two months after the fiscal period end (three months for a CCPC claiming the Small Business Deduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Legal Name and Business Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the limited partnership and 15-character CRA Business Number (Program Account RP0001).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partnerships must appoint a Canadian resident agent, show the agent's name, and obtain a Business Number before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from global EOR payroll administration, contractor placement, and cross-border staffing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source revenue attributable to the partnership's activities; foreign-source revenue allocated to non-resident partners may be excluded under applicable tax treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, wages, contractor payments, pension and benefits, professional fees, rent, technology and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border payments to related non-resident service providers must satisfy the arm's length standard and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1, Line 400 – Net Income (Loss) Before Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss of the partnership before allocation to partners; reconciled to financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net income is allocated to resident and non-resident partners according to the partnership agreement and Schedule 50; non-resident partners are taxed on the Canadian-source share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed after adjustments for non-deductible items, depreciation, and specifically disallowed expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership's taxable income is passed through; non-resident partners compute Part I tax on their share unless treaty relief applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15% on taxable income allocated to corporate partners, or at progressive rates for individual partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners generally file Form T2 for corporate partners or T1 for individuals; treaty benefits must be claimed with the required residency certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month for up to 12 months; late T5013 filing: C$25 per day per partner up to C$2,500; gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated amount; CRA prescribed-rate interest compounds daily.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to non-residents; treaty rates under the Canada-US treaty are 5% for affiliated companies and 15% for portfolio dividends; distributions from a Canadian limited partnership are generally taxed as Part I income at the partner level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide CRA Form NR301 (or NR302 for partnership allocations) and a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence jurisdiction; the Canadian payer may then apply the reduced treaty rate at source; if no certificate is provided, the statutory 25% must be withheld and the non-resident may file Form NR7 to claim a refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for both interest and royalties; Canada-US treaty: 0% on arm's length interest and 10% on industrial royalties; most other Canadian DTAs set interest at 10-15% and royalties at 10-15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1,000,000 aggregate value of cross-border non-arm's length transactions with a related foreign party per taxation year triggers mandatory contemporaneous documentation and the 10% transfer pricing penalty exposure; Country-by-Country Reporting is required for multinational groups with C$750,000,000 or more in consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate offshore Economic Substance Regulations; economic substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the common law sham doctrine, and Income Tax Act s. 247(2) recharacterization powers requiring the EOR partnership to have genuine employees, premises, bank accounts, and non-resident decision-making.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making false statements in T2/T5013 returns, concealing Canadian-source staffing revenue, misclassifying employees as independent contractors, or issuing sham EOR invoices to shift profit offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s. 239(1): fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years; gross negligence penalty of 50% under s. 163(2); full reassessment of tax, interest, and restitution orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general partners, and senior officers who direct or acquiesce in the evasion are exposed to criminal prosecution as parties under Criminal Code ss. 21-22, personal fines, imprisonment, asset seizure, travel bans, and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct or remit federal income tax, CPP, EI, and provincial payroll levies from global contractor and employee wages, or diverting withheld trust funds into operating capital.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s. 227.1 director liability certificates for unremitted amounts; 10% penalty for failure to remit; interest at the prescribed rate compounded daily; CRA garnishment and security demands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are jointly and severally liable for all unremitted source deductions, interest, and penalties; CRA may enforce without a court order, impose asset freezes, and issue travel bans preventing departure from Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a limited partnership or foreign intermediary with no employees, office, bank account, or real EOR business purpose solely to obtain treaty benefits and avoid Part XIII withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalidation of the arrangement under the sham doctrine; GAAR penalty of 25% of the tax benefit; transfer pricing reallocation under s. 247(2); reassessment at the statutory 25% withholding rate plus arrears interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable under s. 160 for transfers to non-arm's length persons and receive court orders to repatriate funds; criminal fraud prosecution is possible when the shell is used to deceive CRA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the EOR and cross-border contractor payroll platform without accurate Money Services Business registration, failing to report suspicious transactions, or operating without a written compliance program under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to C$500,000 for individuals and C$1,000,000 for corporations per violation; criminal liability for money laundering offences carries imprisonment up to 10 years and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may be fined personally, banned from operating financial businesses, and subjected to civil forfeiture; willful blindness to laundering is a predicate offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Limited Partner Control / Loss of Limited Liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A limited partner of the Canadian LP participates in control or management of the EOR business by hiring employees, executing client contracts, or directing payroll operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under each Canadian provincial Limited Partnership Act, the limited partner forfeits the limited liability shield and becomes jointly and severally liable for all partnership debts and tax obligations, including withheld payroll taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The offending limited partner and their corporate directors become personally liable for EOR obligations; CRA and creditors may pursue personal bank accounts, residences, and investments without the normal corporate veil protection.
